description: The repository shall maintain this catalog as the canonical record of Constellation requirements, ownership, implementation evidence, verification, milestones, release scope, sources, and known limitations.
notes: The schema preserves the common Taskyon and Syncpeer columns and adds Taskyon compatibility, milestone, and target-release tracking.

description: A requirement shall not be marked tracked or implemented until its owning implementation path and focused verification evidence are recorded.
notes: Existing Taskyon or Syncpeer behavior is dependency evidence, not Constellation implementation evidence.

description: Every requirement shall classify its relationship to Taskyon as native protocol reuse, layered application behavior, a runtime adapter, or local Constellation behavior.
notes: Allowed values are native, layered, adapter, and local.

description: Requirements shall use foundation, web-preview, 0.1, post-1.0, or future milestones to express implementation order independently from release scope.
notes: A 0.1 requirement may have a foundation or web-preview milestone because target_release defines product inclusion.

description: Every requirement shall use target_release 0.1, post-1.0, or future so the complete feature scope of the first usable release is directly filterable without duplicating the catalog.
notes: Milestone orders implementation; target_release defines product scope.

description: Release 0.1 shall contain the complete first usable product scope; compatible 0.x releases may harden that scope from field evidence, and the same product shall become 1.0 only after satisfactory real-world browser, Android, relay, privacy, battery, and adverse-network validation.
notes: Version 1.0 is a maturity promotion rather than a smaller or separate feature set. Sensor, location, share, and transport wire versions evolve independently from product release numbers.

description: Release 0.1 shall ship the hosted browser app, an installable Tauri Android app, and installable Linux desktop artifacts consisting of an AppImage and a Flathub-ready Flatpak, and shall let two real people use independently generated links to share live locations in either direction across the supported clients, observe freshness and connected viewers, and stop or revoke access without developer tooling.
verification: tests/p2p-share.spec.ts desktop;scripts/test-android-managed.mjs API 29 and API 36 background Android-to-browser relay flows;nix run .#build-appimage and extracted AppImage launch smoke
notes: An Android foreground-service source continues P2P sharing after the Activity goes home, reports a connected viewer, and revokes the session on Android 10 and Android 16 emulators. A distributable AppImage is now produced in dist and its extracted payload remains running through the sandbox launch smoke. Desktop end-to-end location sharing, Flatpak, hosted deployment, browser-to-Android direction, process-restart recovery, signed release, notification-action automation, and two-person physical-device acceptance remain required. Reciprocity uses two independent one-way links; mutual QR pairing is deferred until after 1.0.

description: Constellation shall be distributed under the MIT License with copyright held by Xyntopia.
verification: LICENSE contains the standard MIT License text and Copyright (c) 2026 Xyntopia.
notes: The license applies to the Constellation repository; reused dependencies retain their own licenses.

description: Constellation shall consume versioned Taskyon packages only for shared protocol, P2P, Space, and generic map capabilities; Constellation-owned location behavior shall remain local and the repository shall never import sibling source paths or build artifacts.
notes: Until matching packages are published, Constellation vendors complete provenance-recorded snapshots of @taskyon/protocol and @taskyon/p2p-core as workspace packages. Generic changes are made in Taskyon first and synchronized; released package dependencies replace these snapshots later.

description: Constellation shall use pinned Taskyon-owned TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, and Vite configuration through a supported shared package.
verification: yarn format:check;yarn lint;yarn test;yarn test:android:config;yarn build
notes: The self-contained 0.1 repository pins local configuration aligned with Taskyon and enforces formatting, lint, unit and static Android tests, and the production build in CI. A published Taskyon-owned configuration package remains required to establish one upstream owner and eliminate copied configuration drift.

description: Taskyon shall expose generic MapLibre and PMTiles behavior through a reusable package that does not require the complete Taskyon UI graph or contain location-domain semantics; Taskyon-specific range caching shall remain available through an injected source adapter.
verification: Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre test;Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre typecheck;Taskyon:yarn workspace @taskyon/maplibre build
notes: The generic package is implemented locally but is not published or installed by Constellation. Constellation currently owns its thin map integration and location overlays.

description: A fresh Constellation checkout shall install, test, and build without a Taskyon sibling checkout; future Taskyon integration shall use released package versions rather than workspace links or relative sibling imports.
verification: yarn install --immutable;yarn lint;yarn test;yarn build;yarn test:e2e
notes: Constellation is self-contained through complete vendored Taskyon package snapshots with recorded provenance and documents its standalone web, desktop, and Android workflows. Application code imports package names only; published versions will replace the workspace snapshots without changing imports.

description: Constellation shall supersede the unauthenticated in-memory Deno and SSE location prototype after equivalent basic live sharing is verified.
notes: The prototype remains a UX reference and is not a production compatibility contract.

description: Taskyon shall define a transport-independent read-only sensor service for dynamically described sensors and authenticated observations.
verification: Taskyon:@taskyon/protocol sensor client/server unit test;Taskyon:@taskyon/protocol type-check and build
notes: The versioned descriptor, observation, subscribe, unsubscribe, and event contract exists. Authentication, grants, advertisements, signatures, and peer transport integration remain planned; release 0.1 will expose only Constellation's location profile.

description: A peer shall declare zero or more stable sensor endpoints without requiring a centrally fixed list of sensor kinds.
notes: Declarations are descriptive and grant no authority by themselves.

description: Each sensor endpoint shall identify a versioned profile or canonical schema revision, value shape, units, quality metadata, stream behavior, and owning service principal.
notes: Release 0.1 interprets only the location profile and rejects unsupported required profiles without executing custom semantics.

description: The sensor model shall support interoperable Taskyon standard profiles and dynamically declared custom schemas through the same descriptor mechanism.
notes: Profile interpretation remains separate from transport and discovery.

description: Every observation shall bind its sensor identifier, descriptor revision, source principal, monotonic sequence, capture time, value payload, and quality metadata to an authenticated source envelope.
notes: Receivers reject invalid signatures, schemas, bounds, and replayed or regressing sequences.

description: Authorized consumers shall receive current and subsequent observations through one bounded Taskyon protocol stream with explicit cancellation and backpressure.
notes: Release 0.1 uses one authenticated libp2p stream per viewer with bounded framing and queues, sensor subscribe/unsubscribe, heartbeat cleanup, transport close, and no location persistence.

description: A separately authorized sensor-history capability shall stream a bounded time range without exposing provider paths or an unbounded query surface.
notes: Constellation initially permits at most the latest 30 minutes for remote location views.

description: A signed expiring service advertisement shall identify protocol and descriptor revisions, routing information, limits, and expiry without revealing private Space membership.
notes: Advertisement proves neither authorization nor correct behavior.

description: Space or transient-share grants shall independently authorize publish-own and read-current operations for explicit sensors and bounded scopes.
notes: Read access never implies publication, history access, delegation, device control, or Space administration.

description: Writable attributes and device commands shall remain outside the first sensor protocol and require a separate future command capability and authorization review.
notes: A generic sensor declaration must not become an unrestricted remote-control surface.

description: Sensor endpoint, profile, attribute, and event concepts shall preserve a clean future mapping to Matter while making no initial Matter wire-compatibility claim.
source: Connectivity Standards Alliance Matter specification;Thread Group resources
notes: A Matter bridge will be a separately authorized and tested adapter.

description: Constellation shall treat libp2p as connectivity fabric and the Taskyon sensor protocol as the application layer rather than coupling sensor semantics to one network transport.
notes: This is architectural alignment, not Thread protocol implementation.

description: Constellation shall define a versioned location profile carried inside Taskyon's generic sensor observation payload, including source-owned disclosure precision, bounded coordinates, uncertainty, capture and expiry times, and optional altitude, heading, and speed.
notes: The validated application profile is local to Constellation so Taskyon does not acquire a product-specific location package. Mapping it into the generic Taskyon sensor envelope and peer authorization remain planned.

description: Location observations shall use source-owned monotonic sequences and explicit capture and expiry times so receivers can reject replay and display stale state honestly.
notes: The browser source emits monotonic sequence and explicit capture/expiry times; the viewer rejects non-increasing sequences and recomputes live, delayed, and stale map state. Wall-clock timestamps alone never establish authority.

description: A publishing device shall adapt sampling to movement, elapsed time, requested detail, power state, and a maximum interval through simple battery-versus-detail presets.
notes: Continuous maximum-rate GPS is not the default.

description: The source shall choose exact or approximate disclosure independently for each active share and shall always see the active choice.
notes: New shares default to approximate, exact is explicit, projection happens independently per share, and the active status shows approximate, exact, or mixed precision.

description: For each share using approximate precision, the source shall publish a soft circular uncertainty region with a default one-kilometre radius and keep that region stable while the reported position and its reported GPS uncertainty remain safely contained.
notes: Each in-memory share independently draws cryptographically secure random center and threshold values; there is no grid, reusable seed, share-secret derivation, or per-sample randomization.

description: The source shall create a new randomized uncertainty region only after crossing its private hysteresis threshold consistently, or earlier when needed to preserve containment; consecutive regions shall overlap by at least 75 percent of their area, and poor GPS accuracy shall enlarge the advertised radius rather than exclude the reported uncertainty.
notes: The in-memory browser state uses two consecutive threshold crossings, immediate containment repair, overlap enlargement, and poor-accuracy enlargement. Browser shares intentionally do not resume after restart.

description: Approximate observations shall expose only the advertised region and freshness needed to render it; they shall not expose exact coordinates, grid identifiers, random inputs, private thresholds, speed, or heading.
notes: The published approximate payload contains only the randomized area center, containing radius, source sequence, and freshness timestamps; altitude, heading, speed, threshold, random inputs, and exact coordinates are omitted.

description: The UI and documentation shall state that approximate sharing reduces precision but does not provide anonymity or a formal privacy guarantee, and that long trajectories, known places, screenshots, copied observations, or colluding recipients can still reveal sensitive patterns.
notes: The claim is limited to honest containment of the device-reported coordinate and uncertainty. The map presents the result as a soft area rather than an exact displaced point.

description: A viewer shall distinguish live, delayed, stale, expired, revoked, and unavailable location state instead of silently presenting old coordinates as current.
notes: Age and source expiry remain visible on the map and member surface.

description: Constellation shall present one local person identity with independently named and revocable device identities, each of which may publish its own authorized location.
notes: A device identity does not independently grant broad access to user or Space data.

description: A new source or viewer shall receive a local device identity without registration, hosted account authentication, or disclosure of a stable identity to other link recipients.
notes: Deleting local application data may destroy the local identity and active shares; account recovery is outside 0.1.

description: Background publishers shall receive a narrow device-bound principal and publish-own grant without receiving Space administration or read access to unrelated sensors.
notes: This is the unattended-service boundary used while the phone is locked.

description: Missing membership, grant, publication, or distribution policy shall deny location access.
notes: Global discovery never advertises Space membership.

description: The initial UI shall expose shares and connections rather than requiring users to understand Space keys, overlays, grants, or service advertisements.
notes: Security mechanics remain inspectable in diagnostics and advanced details.

description: A future named family or friends group shall be an independent collaborative Space rather than an extension of the user's default personal Space.
notes: Location publication remains opt-in per Space.

description: Ordinary group members shall be able to publish their own location and view members who currently choose to share, while administrators alone manage membership.
notes: Joining a group never starts location sharing automatically.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support promotion and revocation of multiple administrators and explicit ownership transfer.
notes: Administration remains separate from ordinary membership and device control.

description: Named collaborative Spaces shall support an offline recovery secret without putting root keys or reusable administrator credentials in invitations, links, logs, or QR codes.
notes: Recovery requires bootstrap access to an authorized provider or rendezvous network.

description: Equivalent location data shared into different transient share scopes shall be encrypted independently to reduce provider-side correlation.
notes: Each live share projection is derived from the current source observation and encrypted for only its authorized scope; named Spaces inherit this rule after 1.0.

description: Persistent Space enrollment shall use short-lived single-use QR or invite links with out-of-band fingerprint confirmation and existing-administrator approval.
notes: This enrollment flow is distinct from pre-authorized transient location links.

description: A location link shall create a narrow encrypted share scope and read grant without enrolling receivers as people, devices, or members of a collaborative Space.
notes: Each in-memory share grants only its source location sensor on authenticated per-viewer streams and disappears on page close; named Space integration remains future work.

description: The share URL shall place the bearer capability in its fragment and shall not expose it to HTTP requests, referrers, logs, analytics, or messenger link-preview fetches.
notes: The source peer, reachability addresses, expiry, share identifier, and secret stay in the fragment. The viewer redeems only after explicit acceptance and clears the fragment after success.

description: The web and Android apps shall use the system share surface so a source can send the generated URL through Signal or another installed messenger without messenger-specific account integration.
notes: The web app uses Web Share when available and clipboard copy otherwise. Android system-share verification remains pending.

description: A source shall choose duration, precision, and viewer capacity before generating a link so valid receivers need no later source approval.
notes: Duration, precision, capacity, HMAC redemption, whole-link stop, and automatic expiry are enforced. A per-session revocation control remains unimplemented.

description: A multi-recipient link shall expose only the source's authorized location; receivers shall not discover one another or gain reciprocal sharing automatically.
notes: Two people share in both directions in 0.1 by independently creating one-way links; receivers receive no peer list or reciprocal grant.

description: A source shall be able to show a QR code for the same pre-authorized one-way fragment link, and scanning it shall require explicit receiver acceptance without creating collaborative Space membership.
notes: The QR encodes the exact share URL. Reciprocal pairing remains a separate post-1.0 feature.

description: Sharing shall default to one hour, offer longer presets including eight hours, and stop publication and retrieval automatically at expiry.
notes: The source rejects expired redemption and heartbeat operations, closes expired sessions, and removes expired in-memory shares.

description: An until-revoked link shall exist only as an advanced option behind a prominent warning and explicit source confirmation.
notes: The UI requires fresh acknowledgement, creates a null-expiry grant, and offers whole-share stop. Browser links also end when their source page closes because 0.1 persists no share state.

description: A source shall select a viewer capacity with quick choices of one, ten, and fifty plus an advanced no-share-level-cap option.
notes: Admission enforces the chosen capacity; no-share-level-cap still has a hard runtime ceiling of 128 active sessions.

description: Each successful link redemption shall create a separate ephemeral viewer session so forwarding and concurrent use can be counted, bounded, and revoked.
notes: Each stream gets a nonce-bound HMAC redemption and random in-memory session identifier. Whole-share revocation works; individual session UI remains pending.

description: Viewer sessions shall send bounded heartbeats so the source can see active receiver count, optional receiver-provided labels, ephemeral fingerprints, and last-seen freshness.
notes: The source shows active connected-session count and drops sessions after 35 seconds without a heartbeat. Labels and a detailed last-seen surface remain pending.

description: The source shall be able to revoke one viewer session without revoking every receiver using the same link.
notes: Revocation prevents future access but cannot erase already observed information.

description: The product shall describe active viewers as connected Constellation sessions and shall not claim to count screenshots, copied coordinates, modified clients, or downstream rebroadcasts.
notes: The UI labels the number as connected sessions. It is operational presence, not proof of human attention or non-retention.

description: Two devices shall establish reciprocal view grants through a hidden pair scope after both people independently confirm their own duration and precision.
notes: Stopping or expiring one direction does not silently stop or extend the other direction.

description: The map screen and Android notification shall continuously show whether sharing is active, its recipients or scope, precision, expiry, and a one-action stop control.
notes: The web screen continuously shows active-share and viewer counts and the ready sheet provides one-action whole-share stop. Persistent reopening, precision/expiry detail, per-session stop, and Android notification controls remain pending.

description: Release 0.1 clients and providers shall not persist exact or approximate location observations; an already connected viewer may retain only its latest observation in memory and shall mark it stale when the source becomes unavailable.
notes: A new viewer waits for the source when it is offline; the relay stores no location or history. Encrypted source-side approximation region state is control state rather than an observation and is deleted with its share. Durable self-history and provider-hosted last-known state are deferred until after 1.0.

description: Remote trail access shall expose only bounded viewing streams with no export operation or persistent viewer cache while acknowledging that an authorized viewer can capture rendered data.
notes: The protocol shall not make an unenforceable DRM claim.

description: A device's durable trail shall contain only samples generated by that device and shall never append locations received from another peer.
notes: This prevents ordinary viewers from becoming accidental history replicas or onward publishers.

description: A device shall append self-generated samples to bounded daily text journals containing a versioned header and one authenticated base64url ciphertext envelope per line.
notes: No database is required; plaintext coordinates never enter the journal.

description: Journal envelopes shall authenticate device identity, format version, sequence, capture time, and previous-envelope commitment so truncation, reordering, replay, and corruption are detected.
notes: Recovery may preserve valid prefixes while reporting damaged or missing suffixes.

description: Completed daily or size-bounded journals shall rotate into signed immutable segments suitable for verification and optional blind replication.
notes: Mutable current journals remain local and have one owning writer.

description: Self-history shall default to thirty days and offer shorter periods or keep-until-deleted; cleanup shall remove complete expired segments and their keys or envelopes.
notes: Retention changes do not silently publish or replicate history.

description: Android shall protect the local trail key with Android Keystore so an explicitly started background share can continue after screen lock without exposing a broad Space or user root key.
notes: Behavior after reboot follows platform protected-data availability and fails closed when the key is unavailable.

description: A source shall derive the minimum authorized time range from local self-history and encrypt a separate projection for each Space or transient share scope.
notes: Canonical self-history is never handed directly to a remote provider.

description: Selected storage services may retain opaque source-authored immutable trail segments without receiving plaintext, Space membership, or decryption authority.
notes: Ordinary viewer devices do not satisfy replica durability targets.

description: A source may grant remote viewers access to at most the latest thirty minutes of its trail through a bounded memory-only stream.
notes: The viewer discards the window on close, expiry, or revocation.

description: Official clients shall not write another device's received trail to persistent storage or re-advertise it as a local sensor history.
notes: A malicious authorized client can still capture plaintext and is outside this enforceable guarantee.

description: The web app shall use Taskyon browser libp2p with WebRTC, WebTransport, secure WebSockets, and circuit-relay transport as available.
notes: The browser runtime reserves configured relay reachability, advertises addresses only inside the bearer fragment, and opens one Noise-protected protocol stream per viewer. Transport-specific status detail remains limited.

description: Taskyon P2P shall provide a js-libp2p transport adapter backed by Tauri native sockets so Android is not limited to browser WebRTC connectivity.
notes: The adapter belongs upstream in Taskyon and must preserve the same peer identity and stream semantics.

feature: Native HTTP and secure relay access
description: The Android host shall expose bounded native HTTP or secure WebSocket connectivity needed for bootstrap, relay, and provider access without exposing generic unrestricted network calls to the UI.
notes: Native networking is capability-scoped and uses the same service contracts as web transports.

description: Peers shall try compatible direct transports first and then configured Taskyon circuit relays and gateways with bounded retries and backoff.
notes: The viewer orders non-circuit addresses before circuit addresses and the source tries configured relays. A failed source startup now stops its unreachable peer so the next user attempt creates a fresh peer instead of reusing a dead result. Timed reconnect backoff and a controlled direct-path diagnostic remain pending.

description: Release 0.1 shall operate production bootstrap, rendezvous, secure WebSocket or WebTransport, and circuit-relay endpoints separately from the static web app so browser and Android peers can connect when direct paths fail.
notes: The service deployment is Taskyon-operated, transports only authorization-scoped encrypted traffic, and cannot guarantee networks that block every outbound path.

description: A Space or advanced user shall be able to configure additional bootstrap, relay, and blind-storage providers without replacing the Taskyon protocol.
notes: Provider selection remains separate from service advertisement and authorization.

description: Share and Space traffic shall use cryptographically separate overlays whose identifiers, grants, and contents are absent from global discovery.
notes: Release 0.1 quick shares avoid stable secret-derived discovery tokens and carry reachability plus independent random grant secrets in URL fragments. Full private Taskyon rendezvous remains planned.

description: Hosted relays, mesh routers and Space bridges shall forward opaque end-to-end encrypted traffic without receiving location plaintext, reusable share capabilities, or implicit collaborative Space membership.
notes: A router that decrypts or republishes data is a distinct service principal requiring an explicit grant; ordinary routing never grants sensor access.

description: An authorized blind provider may retain the newest encrypted location observation and its expiry so receivers can distinguish last-known state while the source is temporarily unreachable.
notes: Expired state is unavailable and is removed according to provider policy.

description: The product shall not promise connectivity through total network loss, captive portals, or networks that block every available outbound transport.
notes: Diagnostics identify direct, relayed, offline, blocked, and degraded states.

description: Relays and publishers shall enforce bounded messages, stream counts, heartbeats, quotas, rates, and expiries before allocating unbounded work.
notes: Client frames are limited to 8192 bytes and 32 pending messages, links to four addresses and 1800 fragment characters, sessions to 128, remembered redemption nonces to 1024 per share, and heartbeat/expiry cleanup is bounded. Hosted relay quotas require separate deployment evidence.

description: Future Constellation viewer sessions shall operate unchanged over Taskyon logical streams routed across multiple peer links while preserving per-viewer authorization, counting, expiry, revocation, ordering and explicit route-failure state.
notes: Intermediate routing belongs to Taskyon P2P beneath the sensor protocol. This is not part of release 0.1.

description: Future location sessions shall be able to traverse mixed LAN, Bluetooth, WebRTC, native-socket and relay links without introducing transport-specific location messages or weakening authorization.
notes: Bluetooth and LAN are planned link adapters, not currently implemented transports or claims of Thread, Zigbee or Bluetooth Mesh wire compatibility.

description: A future reachable LAN or mesh gateway shall be able to carry multiplexed upstream traffic and route separate encrypted viewer sessions to several authorized downstream peers without becoming a location viewer by default.
notes: The source retains per-viewer capacity, presence and revocation semantics. Plaintext redistribution requires a separate explicit service grant.

description: Future mesh routing may retain only the newest bounded encrypted location frame across intermittent links and shall discard it at the source-controlled expiry without constructing a trail or durable received-location history.
notes: Blind routers receive no location plaintext. Longer queues and history remain separate capabilities.

description: The primary surface shall be a full-screen share map with one prominent sharing and expiry control and a compact connections drawer.
notes: The map renders local and received current locations, the screen reports P2P/share/viewer state, and the QR sheet offers whole-share stop. A compact connections drawer and per-session controls remain pending.

description: The initial app shall keep the map, active shares, link creation, viewer management, and diagnostics reachable without introducing a broad dashboard.
notes: Creation, explicit acceptance, QR/link sharing, active count, and whole-share stop remain on one screen. Reopening existing links and per-viewer management need a small active-shares surface.

description: Constellation shall provide Taskyon-aligned light and dark palettes, use the operating-system color-scheme preference by default, and react when that system preference changes.
notes: The web shell and MapLibre basemap use the system scheme and react live. Focused browser coverage for a live scheme change remains to be added.

description: Constellation shall interpret its location profile locally and render current points, accuracy or approximate areas, and stale state as generic GeoJSON overlays on MapLibre.
notes: The thin local component preserves standalone builds while the generic Taskyon map package is unpublished. It contains no peer protocol logic and can later be replaced by @taskyon/maplibre without moving location semantics upstream.

description: The map shall use the configured Taskyon PMTiles archive and shall not silently contact a third-party raster-tile fallback.
notes: The local adapter uses only the Taskyon world archive and shows an unavailable-basemap notice on failure. Browser network behavior still requires end-to-end verification.

description: Every successfully requested PMTiles byte range shall be retained through the Taskyon StorageClient range cache under a bounded LRU policy.
notes: No background area or whole-world prefetch is required.

description: The app shall continue to render cached map ranges and location overlays while offline and shall visibly indicate unavailable uncached basemap data.
notes: Location exchange and collection do not depend on map-tile availability.

description: The web application shall use Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Vue Router, and small local UI components without importing the full Quasar application stack.
notes: The browser shell builds without Quasar; Tauri embedding and the shared Taskyon configuration package remain separate planned requirements.

description: Modern mobile and desktop browsers shall create and view shares while the page remains active, and shall clearly report that publication may stop when the browser suspends or closes the page.
notes: The source requests high-accuracy browser geolocation after user action, publishes only while the page owns the runtime, and the UI states that closing the page stops sharing. Reliable background publication still requires Android.

description: The production Vue application shall be deployed as a static site at https://constellation.taskyon.space with SPA routing and share fragments preserved entirely on the client.
notes: The build is compatible with a static host and native share URLs target this origin. Deployment must also publish a matching Android assetlinks.json; the emulator currently reports that verified App Link association as absent.

description: The web build shall be installable as a secure-context PWA while stating that browser background location is not reliable after suspension.
notes: Foreground browser sharing is the supported web guarantee.

description: Release 0.1 shall provide the shared Vue map and foreground location-sharing UI as a usable Tauri desktop application for supported Linux desktops; Android foreground-service controls shall remain unavailable on desktop rather than being presented as supported.
verification: yarn test:unit;cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml;yarn tauri dev;nix run .#build-appimage and extracted payload launch smoke;desktop location-sharing smoke test
source: Tauri desktop platform requirements;Constellation product decisions
notes: Desktop capability selection is explicit and desktop Tauri uses WebView browser geolocation instead of loading the mobile-only plugin. The packaged AppImage payload launches and stays alive through the sandbox smoke window; an end-to-end desktop location-sharing smoke test remains pending.

description: Release 0.1 shall produce a distributable Linux AppImage and a Flatpak package with Flathub-compatible metadata, icons, sandbox permissions, architecture declarations, and reproducible build commands.
verification: scripts/copy-desktop-artifact.test.mjs;nix run .#build-appimage;extracted AppImage payload launch smoke;Flatpak metadata validation
source: Tauri desktop distribution requirements;Constellation product decisions
notes: The isolated Nix FHS builder packages GTK, WebKit, schemas, and AppImage tooling without host-library assumptions and produced dist/constellation-desktop-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage. Tauri frontend assets build into a separate dist-tauri directory so web builds cannot delete packaged artifacts in dist. The extracted AppImage payload stayed alive through a 15-second virtual-display smoke; this sandbox kernel returns ENOENT for the static-PIE AppImage runtime itself, so direct execution still requires validation on a normal Linux host. The Flatpak build remains unverified and its manifest permits network dependency resolution, so pinned offline sources are required before Flathub submission. Signing, update metadata, architecture coverage, and CI publication remain pending.

description: Release 0.1 shall package the shared Vue map and sharing UI as an installable Tauri 2 Android application, with working link and QR flows, foreground viewing and sharing, Android permission handling, and access to the required background-sharing controls; Android-only location, key, socket, notification, and service behavior shall remain behind native adapters.
verification: yarn test:android:config;yarn test:android:managed API 29 and API 36 background Android-to-browser relay flows
notes: The installed Tauri 2 app renders the shared UI, creates a QR/link share through a service-owned peer, collects native service location, and continues relayed publication after the Activity goes home on Android 10 and Android 16 emulators. Verified hosted App Links, first-run background-permission denial automation, release signing, and physical-device evidence remain pending.

description: Explicitly started Android sharing shall continue collection and publication in a foreground service with a persistent status notification and stop action.
verification: scripts/test-android.mjs API 36 Activity-home relay flow;x86_64 debug APK build
notes: The API 36 emulator proves service survival and protocol exchange after the Activity goes home. The persistent notification and stop action compile into the app; automated notification-action, screen-lock, and physical-device battery evidence remain pending.

description: An Android source share shall be owned by the foreground service from creation until stop or expiry; the Activity shall remain a controller/view and shall not create a competing source peer when foreground or background state changes.
notes: Service ownership from creation preserves the link's peer identity and removes routine Activity/service handoff races. Android can still run a separate viewer peer when accepting someone else's link.

description: The foreground service shall persist a bounded encrypted sharing request and recover after process recreation, network change, or Android service restart without extending its original expiry.
notes: The request and status are bounded and Android-Keystore encrypted, and expiry is preserved. The service deliberately fails closed on runtime/process death because peer private-key restoration is not implemented; seamless restart and network-transition recovery remain required.

description: Background sharing shall expose understandable battery and metered-network policy while preserving the user's explicit active-share intent and expiry.
notes: The native service now uses a five-second and five-metre minimum location-update baseline instead of continuous one-second zero-distance GPS requests. Adaptive movement and power presets, metered-network controls, and visible policy pauses remain required.

description: The app shall explain foreground and background location permission separately, degrade safely when either is denied, and never infer consent from Space membership or a prior share.
notes: Share creation requests foreground location after the user action. On Android 13 and newer the native adapter requests notification permission and rejects that start attempt with exact retry guidance, preventing a location foreground service from starting before its notification is allowed. The share sheet explains the all-the-time requirement; if background access is absent, the adapter opens app settings and gives exact return instructions. A dedicated rationale screen, denial automation, and API 29 evidence remain pending.

description: The repository shall provide reproducible Tauri Android development, signed release, artifact-copy, emulator, and physical-device workflows with all publishable artifacts copied into dist.
verification: yarn test:android:config;yarn test:scripts;nix develop --command yarn build:android:dev;yarn test:android:managed;release builder missing-secret fail-closed check
notes: The x86_64 emulator debug build is verified and copied to dist/constellation-android-debug-x86_64.apk; Tauri frontend assets use dist-tauri so subsequent package builds preserve all dist artifacts. The arm64 debug path uses the same build-tools wrapper. The signed arm64 release path requires explicit external signing values, writes only ignored temporary signing properties, rejects unsigned release artifacts, and copies a successful result into dist. A real-key signed build, automatic checksums, CI, and physical-device workflows remain pending; signing credentials stay outside the repository.

description: Approximation region state, share capabilities, viewer sessions, device identities, and background sharing requests shall be authenticated and encrypted before ordinary persistent storage.
notes: Android background requests and status, including the bearer link, use AES-GCM with a non-exportable Android Keystore key. Location observations, approximation state, sessions, and peer identity remain memory-only; durable identity/recovery design remains pending. PMTiles are public map data and use a separate cache policy.

description: Logs, diagnostics, tests, crash reports, URLs, filenames, and CI artifacts shall exclude raw coordinates, bearer fragments, Space secrets, private peer addresses, recovery material, and real personal identifiers.
notes: Tests use synthetic coordinates, identities, and network metadata.

description: Every live location or presence request shall validate the exact grant, sensor, scope, operation, expiry, and resource limits before reading or subscribing to data.
notes: Sensor describe and subscribe reject requests until nonce-bound HMAC redemption succeeds; share existence, expiry, capacity, peer identity, session identifier, and location sensor scope are checked before data access.

description: The UI shall explain that revocation prevents future authorized retrieval but cannot erase coordinates already observed, copied, photographed, or retained by a recipient.
notes: No client-side control can enforce deletion after plaintext has been displayed.

description: Sensor, location, share, and transport contracts shall negotiate explicit versions and reject unsupported required semantics without silently widening access.
notes: Product release 0.1 does not rename Taskyon sensor protocol v1; Constellation location, share, and transport contracts version independently. Peer negotiation and rejection across the network are not integrated; unknown optional sensor profiles remain opaque and non-executable.

description: Focused diagnostics shall prove two browser peers exchange authorized location observations directly when possible and through a local relay fallback.
notes: Browser startup stops the libp2p node when relay-reachable address discovery fails; synthetic reachable and unreachable cases are covered. Two isolated Chromium contexts exchanged a synthetic approximate observation through the configured production circuit relay and verified viewer presence. Local-relay and controlled direct-path coverage remain pending.

description: Tests shall cover URL-fragment secrecy, preview fetches, explicit acceptance, multi-session capacity, expiry, whole-link and per-session revocation, and heartbeat presence.
notes: Fragment-only encoding, malformed/expired rejection, proof binding, explicit acceptance, live redemption, and viewer presence use synthetic inputs. Preview fetch, capacity concurrency, heartbeat timeout, and revocation matrix coverage remain pending.

description: Focused deterministic and property-based tests shall cover stationary stability, GPS jitter, private hysteresis, encrypted restart recovery, at least 75 percent consecutive-region area overlap, poor-accuracy radius enlargement, high-speed movement, containment, and cryptographic-randomness bounds.
notes: Synthetic coordinates and injected randomness only. Protocol, link, log, and public-state inspections shall also prove that approximate shares disclose no exact coordinates, grid identifiers, random inputs, private thresholds, speed, or heading.

description: Tests shall prove unauthorized, expired, revoked, wrong-sensor, wrong-scope, and replayed requests are denied before current location state is read or subscribed.
notes: Capability support and service advertisement alone never authorize access.

description: Tests shall prove equivalent observations produce independently encrypted messages for separate transient share scopes.
notes: Named Space coverage is added with that post-1.0 feature; provider-visible metadata is reviewed for residual size and timing leakage.

description: Tests shall verify journal parsing, authentication, sequence integrity, corruption isolation, rotation, retention deletion, and absence of plaintext coordinates.
notes: Fixtures use synthetic paths, identities, keys, and coordinates.

description: Tests shall request map ranges, disconnect the source, verify cached reuse and eviction limits, and confirm that no third-party tile host is contacted.
notes: Map failure must not stop location collection or exchange.

description: Android tests shall cover foreground-service startup, notification stop, screen lock, Activity ownership, process recreation, reboot, expiry, permission denial, metered policy, power policy, and network transitions.
verification: yarn test:android:managed API 29 and API 36 Activity-home service and relay flows
notes: API 29 and API 36 cover foreground-service startup, Activity-home continuation, viewer presence, and UI revocation. Notification-action, lock, process recreation, reboot, expiry, denial, metered, power, network-transition, and physical-phone evidence remain pending.

description: A browser peer and Android background peer shall exchange the same versioned sensor protocol over direct and relayed paths without platform-specific location semantics.
verification: scripts/test-android.mjs API 36 background Android-to-browser plain circuit-relay flow
notes: The service-owned Android source and host Chromium viewer exchange the same authenticated sensor protocol after the Activity goes home, including viewer presence and revocation. Browser-to-Android, direct-path, process reconnect, and external-consumer conformance coverage remain pending. Plain relay is attempted before WebRTC-over-relay because Android WebView WebRTC negotiation may fail.

description: A self-contained sandbox harness shall build an x86_64 test APK, own API 29 compatibility and API 36 modern AVDs, install and drive the app through ADB and WebView automation, inject synthetic locations, and exchange locations with a host dev server and browser peer through 10.0.2.2 over direct and relayed paths.
verification: yarn test:android:managed API 29 and API 36 Android-to-browser relay flows
notes: The harness builds and copies the x86_64 APK, owns headless API 29 and API 36 AVD lifecycles without touching unrelated devices, provisions a current WebView for API 29, drives the app through redacted CDP diagnostics, injects synthetic coordinates, and verifies relay exchange, viewer presence, and revocation. 10.0.2.2 direct transport, restart, abrupt termination, expiry, and network-transition coverage remain pending.

description: Release diagnostics shall classify direct, relayed, reconnecting, offline, captive-portal, and fully blocked scenarios across representative browser and Android networks.
notes: Failures outside available transports are reported rather than hidden or claimed as supported.

description: Future diagnostics shall route synthetic location sessions across multiple peers and mixed links, including LAN fan-out and intermittent Bluetooth-style hops, and verify loop suppression, duplicate rejection, expiry, revocation, bridge authorization, bounded ciphertext retention and plaintext exclusion at blind routers.
notes: Fixtures use synthetic coordinates, identities and addresses; diagnostics must distinguish logical sessions from selected physical routes.

description: A signed release build shall pass background sharing, lock, reboot, process death, network handoff, battery policy, and long-running expiry scenarios on representative supported physical Android 10 and newer devices before promotion to 1.0.
notes: Emulator-only success is insufficient for background-location, vendor power-management, and radio-transition claims; failures may be corrected through compatible 0.x releases.

description: A fresh checkout shall provide a locked Nix flake development shell containing the Node 22, Rust, Tauri Linux, Playwright runtime, Java 17, and Android API 29 and 36 toolchains required to build and test Constellation without importing another repository's environment.
verification: nix flake check;nix run .#build-appimage;nix develop --command yarn lint;nix develop --command yarn test:e2e;nix develop --command cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml;nix develop --command yarn test:android:config;nix develop --command yarn build:android:dev
notes: The shell provides a direct Yarn shim through pinned Node Corepack, Flatpak build tools, and isolates Playwright's downloaded browser from Nix LD_LIBRARY_PATH while retaining Tauri's Linux libraries. A separate isolated FHS app builds the AppImage with pinned GTK, WebKit, schema, linuxdeploy, and AppImage dependencies; its persistent .tmp caches are excluded from repository lint. Browser E2E is verified in the ordinary shell. The x86_64-linux AppImage and APK build are verified with pinned Node 22.23.2, Rust 1.98.1, Java 17, NDK r28c, and Android API 29 and 36 images. Standard host applications such as Git GUI and Kate are intentionally not provided. .envrc is a local ignored convenience file. Foreign host systems remain unverified.
